niche: a grocery market-data firm's 2027 price index structure: which of eighteen food categories get a stand-alone sub-index, each needing one national change over the 52 weeks to 28 November 2026 that holds within 1.5 points in every store format, when every chain prices an item alike in all its stores and small stores sell their slow lines in few weeks
stakeholder_role: the firm's head of price indices, preparing the index committee's 2027 structure paper

spine.file: scan_movement_2026 (store x item x week sales)
spine.entity: one store's sales of one item in one retail week (units and dollars)

world.geography: Australia (a fictional grocery market-data firm and its partner chains; states and cities real; personas on the en_AU index)
world.org_type: a grocery market-data firm publishing a weekly scanner price index from its partner chains' data

driver: The decisive unit is the one that sets the value: averaging records across setters lets volume moving between dearer and cheaper setters pass for a change in the value, and splitting one setter's single value across its outlets keeps only the outlet-periods with a transaction, so the comparisons lose the slowly traded items and follow the busy ones.
driver_concrete: Every chain prices an item alike in all its stores in a format, so a convenience store that sold none of a slow line in a week still charged the chain's price; matching items store by store drops those weeks and the convenience index follows the fast lines, while pooling an item's sales across the format's chains lets the value chain that joined the panel in July and shoppers' moves between chains read as price falls; following each item at the chain that prices it keeps every comparison and every chain's own price.
stump: A strong analyst builds each format's GEKS-Tornqvist index on items matched store by store, the finest like-for-like (or pools each item's sales across the format's stores), so the convenience change of the categories whose slow lines rose most falls more than 1.5 points under their national change (or the supermarket change reads the July value-chain arrival as a price fall) and the 2027 index publishes the wrong set of categories, when following each item at the chain that prices it publishes the golden set.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every rule and field correctly builds each format's GEKS-Tornqvist index on items matched store by store, keeping only the weeks each store sold an item, and finds several categories' convenience change more than 1.5 points from their national change, so the index publishes fewer categories than the chain-level index, which keeps every week a chain sold the item somewhere at the price it set for all its stores.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each category's price change in each store format with every unsold store-week treated as what it is (a week the store sold none at the chain's known price, not a missing price), the missing-data task type's own object; replacing it with the complete-case store-level match, or with a pooled average that ignores who set each price, changes which categories the national figure holds for.

differentiation.task48: 48 aggregates transactions to a two-sided pair grain so a population its monitor cannot see shows an absolute gap; here the grain is the chain that sets a shelf price for all its stores, and the move keeps the comparisons a finer store grain throws away, revealing no hidden population.
differentiation.task120: 120 v1 builds a percentile unit by a two-hop join of claimed members onto a claiming record; here nothing is joined across units: the move coarsens store rows to the chain that prices them, because a store-level match keeps the chain's price only in the weeks that one store happened to sell the item.

notes: Seed DA14 (header and Situation only): kept the world (a grocery scanner price index from partner chains, GEKS-Tornqvist within store formats), the decision (which categories publish as stand-alone 2027 sub-indices, the rest in other food) and the quantity (whether each category's index holds in every store format, filed as its format changes within 1.5 points of its national change). The seed's matched-pair minimum is a filed rule's execution under the 10/10 rules; the decisive step is re-found in the data's structure (central pricing with sparse small-store sales). Housed in General Statistics (missing data): the setting is retail price statistics.
layer1: chains' weekly feeds with their own week ending days and a resubmitted block kept beside the original (latest load wins)
a partner chain joining the panel in July (its stores enter mid-window)
item codes in two formats across feeds (13-digit with and without a leading zero)
stores re-coded after refits and one store moved between formats on a dated effective date
random-weight fresh lines sold by the kilogram beside packed lines sold by the unit
promotion codes in each chain's own vocabulary
a methodology statement and data dictionary that have to be read
